articles.body:
Restoration games made a statement earlier today to update an old ruling about king arthur. 

King Arthur's ability reads: "When King Arthur attacks, you may BOOST that attack. Play the BOOST card, face down, along with your attack card.
If your opponent cancels the effects on your attack card, the BOOST is discarded without effect."

The last line of the ability is a bit vague, especially when it comes to Arthur's card Excalibur. Excalibur is a 6 value attack with no text. Imagine a scenario where Arthur attacks with Excalibur, boosting it with a boost 3. The defender plays a feint, cancelling the effects on Arthur's card. However, Excalibur has no effects to cancel. So does the boost card get discarded without effect, or does it remain and increase Excalibur to a 9? This question has been brought up many times over the years. Restoration Games initially decided that yes, playing a feint into Excalibur will discard the boost card without effect.

However, they released a statement on their official discord rules library to alter this ruling today. I've attached the image below. 

In summary, if a feint is played against excalibur, it does not cause the boost card to be discarded without effect, as the feint did not cancel any effects (because there were no effects to cancel). So excalibur boosted by 3 will deal 7 damage over a feint. 

This is not an intentional buff to Arthur, it's simply a revisiting of an old ruling that must be changed due to how a new fighter interacts with a similar effect. 

Important interactions to note:

- Excalibur with marvel set items. The +1/+2 items from the marvel sets add an effect to the card, therefore they can still be cancelled by a feint. This has not changed. This does mean that if Arthur attacks with boosted excalibur and uses an item, with the defender playing a feint, the feint cancels the effect added by the item. As the effects on Arthur's card were cancelled, the last line of the ability triggers, causing the boost card to be discarded without effect. So 6 value excalibur boosted by 3 and with a +2 item into feint would typically be an 11 value attack. However feint cancels the item's effect, trigger the last line of Arthur's ability and causing the boost card to be discarded without effect as well, making the final value of Arthur's attack 6, just the printed value. 

- Interaction with Black Widow's "Caught in a web." Caught in a web cancels all after combat effects on the opponent's card. If Arthur attacked with a boosted skirmish, or anything with an after combat effect, caught in a web would cancel that effect and discard the boost card without effect. However if Arthur attacks with boosted Excalibur or boosted Momentous Shift (any card without after combat effects), caught in a web cancels nothing and therefore does not discard the boost value without effect.



I hadn't seen this mentioned yet so I wanted to share it here. This is an errata direct from Restoration Games, but there's no harm in playing with or without this new ruling, do what you want with your sets. This will be the ruling used in future competitive events. We've seen this type of ruling before, most notably changing Beowulf (timing for end of game trigger change), Ghost Rider (clarification that setting his speed to 4 from his ability means it cannot be increased past that), and Dr. Strange (clarification on Mists if the opponent has no remaining versatile or attack cards in deck).

I am not associated with Restoration games but this information is direct from their discord server, where you can find all official rulings and the ruling archive.

articles.body:
I still don’t think he has any shot against wukong. No way around his perfect defences, can’t get past clones. Wukong doesn’t have feints anyway so it didn’t change the matchup.

He certainly has better matchups now though. I just had a nail biter game against him with me as beowulf. I was just barely able to win but it was very close. Arthur had no cards left and I just had a few, but was decked out as well. Super great game. The change really impacted the matchup, and it took a lot of small decisions to get that win. I’m excited for the change, and looking forward to playing him more.

articles.body: Uh oh. I just printed an extra copy of Lady of the Lake and Excalibur and added them to Arthur's deck. After playing multiple games with my new Arthur, he's not high tier but he does pretty good and he feels so much better to play with. I'm averaging three Excalibur attacks per game. This ruling is HUGE. Makes me curious what Arthur will rank at if I play with this rule AND the extra cards. I've always felt Arthur should be a top tier dominator. This will likely do it. I think I'll likely leave the new cards in, but cap Excalibur at two uses. I'll have four cards in the deck that give me a much higher chance of getting Excalibur in hand, and to try to defeat discard effects. I'll say Excalibur can't be used to boost an attack, but could be used to boost movement, and can only be used to attack twice. The extra two cards should help get Excalibur and get a little more movement.

articles.body:
I played as Arthur against Medusa yesterday. I kept my extra copy of Lady of the Lake and Excalibur in the deck. I only allowed myself to play Excalibur twice as an attack, and Excalibur could be used to boost movement but not an attack. Mid-game Merlin schemed for drawing four cards and keeping two. Side by side in that draw were both my Lady of the Lake cards. This is one reason I feel that keeping four cards in the deck that can get Excalibur in hand, is important. They could just as easily have been at the bottom of the deck. Anyway, I was able to get two attacks in with Excalibur. Both attacks boosted by 3. In both cases, Medusa chose high block value to minimize damage, but still got hit hard. The one time I chose to boost an attack later in the game, Medusa canceled the effect and took minimal damage. In the end Merlin swooped in with a ranged attack that did fatal damage to Medusa. The game could have gone either way, as after my second big hit with Excalibur I was at a real card disadvantage and had Medusa pressured me, should could have very possibly destroyed me.

Take aways... With the extra cards Arthur has a much better chance of actually getting to use Excalibur twice in a game. He also has a little more maneuverability or boosted attack power with the extra scheme card. He feels much much much better to play with. It never felt right that he had such low chance of getting two uses out of Excalibur. Too swingy. Boosted attacks are not the strategy for Arthur to win. The only boosted attack that really makes sense is Excalibur. Even limiting myself to that, I hit super-hard, but then find myself at card disadvantage for a few turns. Timing is critical. An early game boosted regroup with a regroup will be phenomenal for the mind-game. Peel away a high-value defense by burning two weak cards and getting one card draw. Then the opponent is guessing what the next boosted attack is.   

I know there are some fighters who can hit very hard if everything lines up. She-hulk has two cards which allow her to burn an action to hit for nine. There are a couple of things that need to line up for her to get that hit, and it can be canceled, but she quite often does succeed in pulling it off. Dracula's beastform is super-lethal when he has a hand full of cards and catches the enemy with no cancel and a low hand to hit back. It's a costly attack but very powerful. Bigfoot slings logs regularly and easily. Medusa has her gaze of stone. Deadpool has one big attack combo that is pretty easy to pull off. Quite a few fighters have a couple of signature big hits. It has always felt off to me that Arthur only has one Excalibur and that it's quite possible to not see it or only see it once in a game. The extra Excalibur and Lady of the Lake fix that. He now hits like a freight train, as he should. He becomes legitimately scary to face. 

If I did not have the extra cards in my deck, what would I do? I like the rule somebody came up with that if Lady of the Lake is played to get Excalibur out of the deck, then Lady of the Lake get shuffled back into the deck. This allows the possibility of getting her and Excalibur for a second time. But better still, print an extra copy of those two cards and add them to your deck. It makes Arthur feel a lot more like he ought to feel.

articles.body:
[q="RaistlinMajere"][q="tigerhollytimes"]
I saw the official change (finally!), but I haven't tried it yet. It's interesting, but at first glance it seems like a rather minor change.
[/q]

Arthur isn't any stronger against opponents who could never cancel his attacks, but for those who could. This change opens up a whole new avenue of mind games for Arthur. 

His opponent still very badly wants to cancel a boosted Momentous shift that could be ( 5 + 3 ) = 8 value attack if Arthur moved that turn. Successfully canceling that turns it into a 3. 

But now that you can end up receiving an uncancellable 9 value excalibur instead, which does 7 damage on top of a feint's 2 defense value. 

Its too bad Arthur is so susceptible to discard, because now its seems like you might handicap yourself a bit if you play both of your Excalibur's twice in a game too early, because then the opponent knows its always safe to feint every other boosted attack.

articles.body: Hi, people! It's been six months since this buff. It's clear that Arthur hasn't reached the level of the big three, but that's not necessary. I love this character (as do many other players) despite the fact that he wasn't as powerful, and so this buff hasn't left me indifferent. Share your experience: how much stronger has the King become in your lobby (he's become a decent mid-tier player at our table)? I'm only interested in the official update and your emotions after playing with these changes!)
articles.bodyXml:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<xml><safehtml>Hi, people! It's been six months since this buff. It's clear that Arthur hasn't reached the level of the big three, but that's not necessary. I love this character (as do many other players) despite the fact that he wasn't as powerful, and so this buff hasn't left me indifferent. Share your experience: how much stronger has the King become in your lobby (he's become a decent mid-tier player at our table)? I'm only interested in the official update and your emotions after playing with these changes!)</safehtml></xml>

articles.body: He is exactly the same. Like I said on every topic that suggested this as a buff, his main problem is losing important cards of which he has single copies, and slow speed. He get's dropped lowish and then kited to death.
